 Honda and Acura Brands Announce 635,808-Vehicle Recall To Address Software Issue
 An error in the Driver Attention Monitor road-condition compensation calculation can leave drivers without power steering assistance 
 Published: 12 Nov 2026, 19:08 UTC 
 By: 
 Mircea Panait 
   9 photos Photo: Acura 
 American Honda Motor is recalling a whopping 635,808 automobiles in the United States market. An electronic power steering software error is capable of disabling power steering assistance without warning, increasing the risk of a crash. The problem affects three models, namely the discontinued TLX sedan, the MDX crossover, and the mechanically similar Pilot. 
 Affected model years range from 2021 for the Acura TLX all the way to 2025 for the Honda Pilot. Referred to as 26V721 by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, this recall is designated KQB and TQA by the Japanese automaker. Not surprising in the least, the family-oriented Pilot crossover accounts for the majority of the recall population.
 383,110 such vehicles are involved, while Acura contributed another 177,100 units of the MDX and 75,598 for the less popular TLX. When it comes to production timeframes, make that August 11, 2020, through December 23, 2025. Because it's very hard to find out when a subject vehicle has been produced, customers are better off simply checking the VIN against the NHTSA's database.
 American Honda Motor puts the blame on the software developed by Robert Bosch Automotive Steering LLC of Florence, Kentucky. The software in question contains an error in the Driver Attention Monitor's road-condition compensation calculation. Under specific operating conditions, the system may attempt a floating-point division by zero. I'm no math expert or computer scientist, but a quick search on Google reveals that downstream logic failures are possible.
 The EPS software responds to the calculation error by shutting down power steering assistance, thus entering failsafe mode. Drivers may retain the mechanical connection between the steering wheel and the front wheels, but no power assistance means a lot more muscle to turn the front wheels as intended.
 Photo: Acura 
Additional steering effort without warning is the kind of situation that greatly increases the risk of a crash, especially when cornering at high speeds. In the event of a power steering assistance malfunction, the EPS warning light illuminates. Honda started looking into this matter in November 2021, and more reports followed through August 2025.
 Engineers and technicians, however, struggled to pinpoint the root cause through returned components. Honda argues that dealers or the supplier had deleted the relevant error codes from returned parts. Bosch ultimately identified the problem in August 2025, then Honda recreated the issue in December 2025. Back in February 2026, the investigation established that the failure occurs in very specific operating conditions.
 After collecting more info through the spring and the summer, American Honda Motor ultimately determined that said issue constitutes a defect related to motor vehicle safety. No fewer than 146 warranty claims have been filed thus far, and Honda is aware of an injury report as well.
 Said report and the warranty claims were filed in the period from May 22, 2022, through October 22, 2026. The fix, meanwhile, involves new code for the EPS control unit. Dealers are much obliged to install the new software package through the OBD-II port at no charge to affected customers.
 Owners and lessees will be notified in December, with Honda targeting December 14, 2026. The NHTSA's database contains all subject VINs as of this writing.
